# Dot-com vs AI Bubble Comparison Dataset

## Overview
Four datasets capturing key market metrics across two technology-driven market booms: the 1997–2002 dot-com era and the 2021–2024 AI era. The data is structured for side-by-side temporal alignment using a common `quarter_offset` or `year` field within each era.

## Data Source

### nasdaq_index
Quarterly NASDAQ Composite closing values, rebased to 100 at the start of each era. Fields: `era` (string: "Dot-com" or "AI"), `quarter_offset` (integer 0–23), `label` (calendar quarter string), `index_value` (float). The dot-com series spans 24 quarters (1997-Q1 to 2002-Q4); the AI series spans 16 quarters (2021-Q1 to 2024-Q4).

### pe_ratio
Trailing 12-month P/E ratio for the NASDAQ Composite, sampled at irregular quarterly intervals. Fields: `era`, `quarter_offset`, `label`, `pe` (float, ratio). Dot-com P/E ranges from ~28 to ~105; AI-era P/E ranges from ~24 to ~40.

### ipo_counts
Annual count of technology-sector IPOs on US exchanges. Fields: `era`, `year` (integer), `ipo_count` (integer). Dot-com era: 6 years; AI era: 4 years.

### corporate_earnings
Aggregate annual net income for NASDAQ-100 companies in nominal billion USD. Fields: `era`, `year`, `earnings_bn` (float; may be negative). Dot-com earnings range from −12.3 to 30.5 B; AI-era earnings range from 358 to 510 B.

## Data Notes
- NASDAQ index values are rebased independently per era; absolute levels differ dramatically.
- P/E ratios for the dot-com era include periods of near-zero aggregate earnings, inflating the ratio.
- Nominal earnings are not inflation-adjusted; direct magnitude comparison across eras should note the ~20-year gap.
- 2024 figures are estimates based on analyst consensus as of late 2024.

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import json
from pathlib import Path

data=json.loads(Path('/app/benchmark/source_data.json').read_text())

nas=data['nasdaq_index']['data']
pe=data['pe_ratio']['data']
ipo=data['ipo_counts']['data']
earn=data['corporate_earnings']['data']

# Prepare series
series={}
for era in ['Dot-com','AI']:
    rows=sorted([r for r in nas if r['era']==era], key=lambda r:r['quarter_offset'])
    x=np.array([r['quarter_offset'] for r in rows])
    y=np.array([r['index_value'] for r in rows])
    series[era]={'x':x,'y':y,'labels':[r['label'] for r in rows]}

pe_series={}
for era in ['Dot-com','AI']:
    rows=sorted([r for r in pe if r['era']==era], key=lambda r:r['quarter_offset'])
    pe_series[era]={'x':np.array([r['quarter_offset'] for r in rows]),
                    'y':np.array([r['pe'] for r in rows])}

# annual mapping to quarter_offset (start year per era)
start_year={'Dot-com':1997,'AI':2021}

def annual_to_qoff(era, year):
    return (year-start_year[era])*4 + 1.5  # mid-year around Q2/Q3

ipo_series={}
for era in ['Dot-com','AI']:
    rows=sorted([r for r in ipo if r['era']==era], key=lambda r:r['year'])
    ipo_series[era]={'x':np.array([annual_to_qoff(era,r['year']) for r in rows]),
                     'y':np.array([r['ipo_count'] for r in rows]),
                     'year':[r['year'] for r in rows]}

earn_series={}
for era in ['Dot-com','AI']:
    rows=sorted([r for r in earn if r['era']==era], key=lambda r:r['year'])
    earn_series[era]={'x':np.array([annual_to_qoff(era,r['year']) for r in rows]),
                      'y':np.array([r['earnings_bn'] for r in rows]),
                      'year':[r['year'] for r in rows]}

# Peaks for markers
peaks={}
for era in ['Dot-com','AI']:
    i=np.argmax(series[era]['y'])
    peaks[era]=(series[era]['x'][i], series[era]['y'][i], series[era]['labels'][i])

# Colors (editorial)
COL_DOT = '#1f77b4'   # deep blue
COL_AI  = '#d62728'   # muted red
GREY='#4d4d4d'
GRID='#d9d9d9'

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.size': 10,
    'axes.titlesize': 12,
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 9,
    'axes.edgecolor': '#333333',
    'axes.linewidth': 0.8,
    'xtick.color': '#333333',
    'ytick.color': '#333333',
    'text.color': '#222222',
    'axes.facecolor': 'white',
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
})

fig=plt.figure(figsize=(12.5,7.5), dpi=200)
# grid spec
from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec

gs=GridSpec(2,2, height_ratios=[2.2,1.3], width_ratios=[1.25,1.0], hspace=0.35, wspace=0.25)

# Top-left: NASDAQ rebased + earnings backdrop
ax=fig.add_subplot(gs[0,0])
ax2=ax.twinx()

# Earnings as semi-transparent bars (separate per era with slight offset)
barw=0.8
# offset bars so they don't overlap completely
ax2.bar(earn_series['Dot-com']['x']-0.25, earn_series['Dot-com']['y'], width=barw*0.45, color=COL_DOT, alpha=0.18, label='Dot-com earnings')
ax2.bar(earn_series['AI']['x']+0.25, earn_series['AI']['y'], width=barw*0.45, color=COL_AI, alpha=0.18, label='AI earnings')

# NASDAQ lines
ax.plot(series['Dot-com']['x'], series['Dot-com']['y'], color=COL_DOT, lw=2.3, label='NASDAQ (rebased) — Dot-com')
ax.plot(series['AI']['x'], series['AI']['y'], color=COL_AI, lw=2.3, label='NASDAQ (rebased) — AI')

# Peak markers
for era, col, txt in [('Dot-com',COL_DOT,'Dot-com peak\n(Mar 2000)'), ('AI',COL_AI,'AI-era high\n(latest in data)')]:
    xpk, ypk, lab = peaks[era]
    ax.scatter([xpk],[ypk], s=35, color=col, zorder=5, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.8)
    ax.axvline(xpk, color=col, lw=1.0, alpha=0.35)
    ax.annotate(txt, xy=(xpk, ypk), xytext=(xpk+0.7, ypk+10 if era=='Dot-com' else ypk+7),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=col, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
                fontsize=9, color=col, ha='left', va='bottom')

ax.set_title('Dot-com (1997–2002) vs AI era (2021–2024): aligned market boom “shape”')
ax.set_xlabel('Quarter offset from era start (0 = first quarter)')
ax.set_ylabel('NASDAQ Composite, rebased (index = 100 at start of era)')
ax2.set_ylabel('NASDAQ-100 aggregate net income (USD billions, nominal)')

ax.grid(True, axis='y', color=GRID, lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 23.5)
# Earnings axis: allow negative to show dot-com 2001
ax2.set_ylim(-50, 560)

# Build combined legend for top-left
handles1, labels1 = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
handles2, labels2 = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Keep only two earnings items but label clearly
leg=ax.legend(handles1 + [handles2[0], handles2[1]],
              labels1 + ['Earnings — Dot-com (RHS)', 'Earnings — AI (RHS)'],
              loc='upper left', frameon=False, ncol=1)

# Top-right: P/E ratios (overlay)
ax_pe=fig.add_subplot(gs[0,1])
ax_pe.plot(pe_series['Dot-com']['x'], pe_series['Dot-com']['y'], color=COL_DOT, lw=2.2, marker='o', ms=3.2, label='Dot-com')
ax_pe.plot(pe_series['AI']['x'], pe_series['AI']['y'], color=COL_AI, lw=2.2, marker='o', ms=3.2, label='AI')

# Highlight dot-com peak P/E
dot_pe_peak=max([r for r in pe if r['era']=='Dot-com'], key=lambda r:r['pe'])
ai_pe_peak=max([r for r in pe if r['era']=='AI'], key=lambda r:r['pe'])
ax_pe.scatter([dot_pe_peak['quarter_offset']],[dot_pe_peak['pe']], s=45, color=COL_DOT, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.8, zorder=5)
ax_pe.scatter([ai_pe_peak['quarter_offset']],[ai_pe_peak['pe']], s=45, color=COL_AI, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.8, zorder=5)
ax_pe.annotate('Dot-com peak\nP/E 105.2', xy=(dot_pe_peak['quarter_offset'], dot_pe_peak['pe']),
               xytext=(dot_pe_peak['quarter_offset']-3.5, dot_pe_peak['pe']+8),
               arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=COL_DOT, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
               fontsize=9, color=COL_DOT, ha='right')
ax_pe.annotate('AI-era high\nP/E 40.3', xy=(ai_pe_peak['quarter_offset'], ai_pe_peak['pe']),
               xytext=(ai_pe_peak['quarter_offset']-4.5, ai_pe_peak['pe']+6),
               arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=COL_AI, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
               fontsize=9, color=COL_AI, ha='right')

ax_pe.set_title('Valuation: trailing P/E (NASDAQ Composite)')
ax_pe.set_xlabel('Quarter offset from era start')
ax_pe.set_ylabel('P/E ratio (x)')
ax_pe.set_xlim(-0.5, 23.5)
ax_pe.set_ylim(0, 115)
ax_pe.grid(True, axis='y', color=GRID, lw=0.8)
ax_pe.legend(title='Era', frameon=False, loc='upper left')

# Bottom: IPO counts as lollipop / bars by year aligned to quarter offset
ax_ipo=fig.add_subplot(gs[1,:])

# baseline
ax_ipo.axhline(0, color='#333333', lw=0.8)

# Plot lollipops per era
for era, col, yoff in [('Dot-com', COL_DOT, -0.12), ('AI', COL_AI, 0.12)]:
    x=ipo_series[era]['x']
    y=ipo_series[era]['y']
    # stems
    for xi, yi in zip(x,y):
        ax_ipo.plot([xi, xi], [0, yi], color=col, lw=2.0, alpha=0.65)
    ax_ipo.scatter(x, y, s=55, color=col, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.8, zorder=5, label=era)

# annotate peaks
dot_ipo_peak=max([r for r in ipo if r['era']=='Dot-com'], key=lambda r:r['ipo_count'])
ai_ipo_peak=max([r for r in ipo if r['era']=='AI'], key=lambda r:r['ipo_count'])
ax_ipo.annotate('Dot-com peak\n308 IPOs (1999)',
                xy=(annual_to_qoff('Dot-com', dot_ipo_peak['year']), dot_ipo_peak['ipo_count']),
                xytext=(annual_to_qoff('Dot-com', dot_ipo_peak['year'])-2.2, dot_ipo_peak['ipo_count']+35),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=COL_DOT, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
                fontsize=9, color=COL_DOT, ha='right')
ax_ipo.annotate('AI-era peak\n198 IPOs (2021)',
                xy=(annual_to_qoff('AI', ai_ipo_peak['year']), ai_ipo_peak['ipo_count']),
                xytext=(annual_to_qoff('AI', ai_ipo_peak['year'])+2.0, ai_ipo_peak['ipo_count']+30),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=COL_AI, lw=0.8, alpha=0.7),
                fontsize=9, color=COL_AI, ha='left')

ax_ipo.set_xlabel('Quarter offset from era start (year points shown at mid-year)')
ax_ipo.set_ylabel('IPO count (annual)')
ax_ipo.set_xlim(-0.5, 23.5)
